title: Two-dimensional percolation with algebraically decaying interactions II: Critical exponents in the long-range regime
authors: Ziyu Liu, Tianning Xiao, Zhijie Fan, Youjin Deng
abstract: We present a comprehensive Monte Carlo study of two-dimensional bond percolation with algebraically decaying connection probabilities $p(r)\propto 1/r^{2+σ}$, establishing the universality diagram in the long-range (LR) regime for $σ\le2$. Using the event-based ensemble method, we simulate systems with linear sizes up to $L=16384$ and investigate three universality regimes: LR Wilson--Fisher (WF) A ($1<σ\le2$), LR Wilson--Fisher B ($2/3<σ\le1$), and LR mean-field (MF) ($0<σ\le2/3$). In the LR-WF-B regime, the anomalous dimension is consistent with $η=2-σ$, in agreement with mathematical results for $2/3<σ<1$, while the correlation-length exponent $ν(σ)$ exhibits nontrivial, non-Gaussian variation. In the LR-WF-A regime, although $η$ remains close to $2-σ$ for smaller $σ$, statistically resolvable deviations $δη(σ)=η-(2-σ)>0$ start to appear near $σ\simeq3/2$ and grow toward the short-range crossover at $σ=2$. Finally, by complementing the event-based simulations with conventional ensemble simulations, we reveal the coexistence of complete-graph asymptotics and LR Gaussian-fixed-point scaling in the LR-MF regime. These results further clarify the critical properties in long-range percolation and provide crucial benchmarks for long-range statistical systems.
summary: This paper performs extensive Monte Carlo simulations to map out the critical behavior of 2D bond percolation with long-range, algebraically decaying interactions. It identifies three distinct universality regimes based on the decay exponent $\sigma$. The work is significant for clarifying how critical properties transition between different scaling behaviors, such as Gaussian Fixed Point and Complete Graph asymptotics, in long-range statistical systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the critical exponents and universality diagram for two-dimensional bond percolation when the interaction decay is algebraic, $p(r) \propto 1/r^{2+\sigma}$.
main_result: The study establishes three distinct universality regimes (LR-WF-A, LR-WF-B, LR-MF) and finds that global observables can exhibit coexistence between Complete-Graph asymptotics and Long-Range Gaussian-Fixed-Point scaling.
method: The research employs comprehensive Monte Carlo simulations using the event-based ensemble method, supplemented by conventional ensemble simulations and finite-size scaling analysis.
model_or_system: The model is two-dimensional bond percolation on a lattice where the connection probability decays algebraically with distance $r$ according to $p(r) \propto 1/r^{2+\sigma}$.
key_observables:
Critical exponents, specifically the anomalous dimension ($\eta$) and the correlation-length exponent ($
u(\sigma)$), are key observables.
important_parameters: The interaction decay exponent $\sigma$ is the primary tuning parameter, defining regimes such as $1 < \sigma \leq 2$ (LR-WF-A) and $0 < \sigma \leq 2/3$ (LR-MF).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of different scaling theories (Wilson-Fisher, Gaussian Fixed Point, Complete Graph) depending on the value of $\sigma$.
figures_summary: Figures are expected to show the universality class diagram in the $(d, \sigma)$ plane and plots comparing calculated critical exponents ($\eta$ vs $\sigma$) against theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the critical behavior across different $\sigma$ regimes, presenting quantitative results in tables detailing fits for various susceptibilities ($\Delta, S_2, \chi_k$) across different $\sigma$ values.
why_interesting: While focused on classical percolation, the study of critical exponents and universality classes in long-range interacting systems provides crucial benchmarks for understanding critical phenomena in many-body quantum systems where interactions decay slowly.
